findings.title: Unparenthesized OR fragment breaks caller AND filters
findings.body: In packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts, getBaseConditions returns the authorization fragment as-is when there are no service filters (line 75). Team and org scope build that fragment as `(teamPredicate) OR (userPredicate)` with no parentheses around the whole OR (the reduce at lines 171-174 and 204-207). SQL AND binds tighter than OR, so the intended caller query `WHERE ${await service.getBaseConditions()} AND "startTime" >= ${start} AND "startTime" < ${end}` is parsed as team-bookings OR (personal-bookings AND date window). Every matching team booking is returned regardless of the date filter, and any other AND predicate appended by the caller (status, member, and so on) is skipped on the team-booking branch. That over-returns rows, ignores the insights time window, and can defeat caller-side restrictions. The same shape exists on the event-type filter at line 106 (`eventTypeId = X OR eventParentId = X`) if getFilterConditions is embedded directly. The old Prisma `AND: [...]` where input did not have this trap, and getBaseConditions already parenthesizes when it combines auth and filters (line 73) but not when it returns auth alone. Wrap every returned fragment, including the OR reduce result, in parentheses so external AND/OR composition is safe.

findings.title: ANY() on a JS array is not a Postgres int array
findings.body: In packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts, org and team authorization interpolate JavaScript number arrays into PostgreSQL ANY() at lines 164 (`"teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})`), 168 (`"userId" = ANY(${uniqueUserIds})`), and 201 (`"userId" = ANY(${userIdsFromTeam})`). Prisma `$queryRaw` / `Prisma.sql` does not encode a JS array as a PostgreSQL `int[]`; the array is one untyped parameter, typically sent as text. PostgreSQL then fails the statement with an error such as `operator does not exist: integer = text` or `op ANY/ALL (array) requires array on right side`. User scope only uses scalar binds, and the only test that executes SQL is user-scoped, so this is not caught. Team and org insights, the main authorization paths, will throw instead of returning bookings. Build the list with Prisma.join and an explicit cast, for example `"userId" = ANY(ARRAY[${Prisma.join(userIds)}]::int[])`, and keep the empty-list guard because Prisma.join([]) is invalid SQL.

findings.title: toEqual on nested Prisma.sql fragments will fail
findings.body: In packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts, the team-scope assertion at line 295, the org-scope assertion at line 332, and the combined-filter assertion at line 429 expect `toEqual` against one flat `Prisma.sql` template. The service does not build those fragments as a single template: buildTeamAuthorizationCondition, buildOrgAuthorizationCondition, and buildFilterConditions nest fragments with `Prisma.sql`(${acc}) OR/AND (${condition})``. Prisma stores nested `Sql` objects in `values` and only flattens them when the query runs, so Vitest deep equality fails even when the rendered SQL matches. The PR notes these tests were not executed. User-scope and single-filter assertions can pass only because those paths return one uncomposed template. Compare a flattened statement, or assert on rows from an executed query, instead of `toEqual` on the `Sql` object; otherwise CI fails and the team/org SQL is never actually checked.
